item.title: Arc red pencilfish
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

The Arc red pencilfish is a small pencilfish in which the space between the black lengthwise stripes is colored red (［16］［19］). Japanese articles introduce it as expensive, because it is very hard to breed and only wild fish (fish collected in the wild) are on the market: “One reason it is rare is that breeding it is very difficult.” (translated) (［18］).

item.title: Australian lungfish
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

The Australian lungfish is a large lungfish that lives only in a few rivers of Queensland, Australia. In Japan it is called「ネオケラ」(Neokera) and is known as a very expensive fish. Japanese blogs and articles say that very few are imported, and that the fish available in Japan have a microchip inside (［12］〜［14］).

item.title: Diamond polka dot stingray
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

The Diamond polka dot stingray (“Diamond polka” for short) is a South American freshwater stingray with white polka dots scattered over a black body (［14］［17］). One Japanese article writes that its price stands out even among freshwater stingrays: “Even cheap ones cost several hundred thousand yen, and expensive ones as much as several million yen.” (translated) (［16］).

item.title: Gilled lungfish
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

Protopterus amphibius, the gilled lungfish, is one of the African lungfishes. A Japanese article introduces it as the smallest species in this group, native to the coast of East Africa, and writes, “Only a few juveniles are imported when the season comes, so it is rarer than other lungfishes.” (translated) (［19］).

item.title: New black cherry tetra
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

The New black cherry tetra is a small characin about 3 cm long whose tail fin is tinged with red (［4］［9］). A Japanese article lists this fish as one of the rare tropical fish that are seldom on the market, and writes, “However, few are in circulation, and it is expensive and rare.” (translated) (［4］).

item.title: Peru glass tetra
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

The Peru glass tetra is a small characin whose body is as clear as glass. A Japanese article introduces it as native to Peru, about 4 cm long, hardy and easy to keep, and then writes, “Like other rare tropical fish, it is a species that is difficult to breed.” (translated), presenting this as the reason its price is on the high side (［9］).

item.title: Saddled bichir
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

Polypterus endlicherii is a large member of the bichirs (Polypterus), the ancient fishes of Africa, whose lower jaw sticks out beyond the upper jaw. A Japanese article introducing rare tropical fish puts it first of its 10 species, and writes, “Not many are traded, and they are not often handled except at fairly large aquarium shops.” (translated) (［17］).

item.title: Tucano tetra
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

The Tucano tetra is a very small characin that does not reach 2 cm in body length even as an adult. Japanese articles introduce it as “a rare fish that lives in a very limited part of the Uaupés River basin” (translated) in Brazil (［13］), and one article writes, “There are tropical fish that are ranked as rare because few reach Japan and they are hard to breed.” (translated) (［14］). Yet after collecting the records, it turned out that neither “how rare is it?” nor “is its habitat really small?” is clear. This page checks what lies behind those claims.

item.title: Zebra pleco
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

The zebra pleco is a small pleco about 7–8 cm long, with black stripes running across a white body (［6］［7］). Japanese articles introduce it as one of the “rare fish”, and write that breeding is difficult and the price is quite high (［20］). About wild fish (fish caught in the wild), one article writes, “Wild fish in particular can fetch around 100,000 yen each, so it can be called a fish of high rarity value.” (translated) (［19］).

item.title: Corydoras "Zebrina" (CW111)
item.description:
1. Introduction — how this page was made

Corydoras “Zebrina” is a fish that sells for tens of thousands of yen a pair, and wild fish can go for more than 100,000 yen. Yet little information is available in Japanese, and some shop descriptions come with a caveat that its breeding method “is presumed to be similar to other common Corydoras” (translated) (product page of a Japanese shop［28］; checked November 16, 2026).
